why:
RE-READ 2026-10-29 (issue 2136), still declined -- for the narrower reason `c:take_request_with_info` gives. The ABI now has the pair: the vtable grew `take_response_with_info` (`rmw_vtable.h`), zenoh, Cyclone DDS and XRCE-DDS fill it, and the runtime dispatches it, so a C program DOES get a reply's `rmw_request_id_t` -- through its callback, `rclc_executor_add_client_with_request_id` (see `c:executor_add_client_with_request_id`) -- and a Rust one the full `ServiceInfo` (`Promise::take_with_info`). WHAT STAYS DECLINED is the rcl POLLING entry point itself, `rcl_take_response_with_info`: its siblings `rcl_take_request` / `rcl_take_response` are not offered (`rcl_compat.h` section 5), and a `_with_info` twin of an absent family is the accessor-without-a-family RFC-0089 warns against.

EARLIER TEXT (superseded, 2026-09-23): RE-VERDICTED 2026-09-23 (phase-444 ledger re-read), gap -> declined. The client side of `c:take_request_with_info`: same declared omission, same two corrections to the 2026-09-21 pass (its `take_with_info` citation is about the SUBSCRIPTION slot and says nothing about this one).

ONE THING IS NOT SYMMETRIC, measured 2026-09-23. On the SERVER side the sequence reaches the C caller; on the CLIENT side it does not. Neither `rclc_client_take_response(client, data, capacity, *len)` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/rclc/detail/nros_generated.h:7768`) nor `rclc_polling_client_take_response_raw(client, buf, buf_len)` (`:7668`) returns one, although the vtable slot beneath them does (`packages/core/nros-rmw-abi/include/nros/rmw_vtable.h:374-388` — `*seq_out` is the id of the request the reply answers, issue 0778's other half). It is dropped on purpose: a nano-ros client keeps ONE call in flight, so there is nothing to correlate a reply against. See `cpp:Client::prune_pending_requests` for that model and `rust:RequestId` for the divergence that would change it.
